title: General-purpose iO from plain LWE
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Construct iO for all polynomial-size Boolean circuits from ordinary polynomially hard LWE, without additional evasive, circular, equivocal, pairing, or knowledge assumptions.
status: General iO has multi-assumption constructions; the 2025 lattice route still requires Equivocal LWE and NTRU-related machinery.
why: It would put general software obfuscation on a widely studied post-quantum foundation.
key_works: Jain–Lin–Sahai (2021), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Well-Founded Assumptions*, ePrint 2020/1003; Cini–Lai–Woo (2025), *Lattice-based Obfuscation from NTRU and Equivocal LWE*, ePrint 2025/1129.

title: General-purpose iO from one-way functions
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Construct general circuit iO from arbitrary one-way functions, allowing genuinely non-black-box constructions and reductions.
status: Existing black-box limitations do not establish an unrestricted impossibility theorem.
why: This would sharply reduce the assumptions needed for the entire obfuscation application ecosystem.
key_works: Asharov–Segev (2015), *Limits on the Power of Indistinguishability Obfuscation and Functional Encryption*, ePrint 2015/341.

title: Unrestricted iO without subexponential hardness
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Obtain unrestricted circuit iO from polynomially hard, independently studied assumptions, avoiding complexity leveraging that requires subexponential security.
status: Polynomial-hardness progress for proof-restricted obfuscation does not itself construct unrestricted iO from polynomially hard conventional assumptions.
why: It could substantially reduce the gap between asymptotic existence and meaningful parameters.
key_works: Jain–Lin–Sahai (2021), ePrint 2020/1003; Dujmovic–Hsieh–Jain–Quach (2026), *How to use Polynomially-Hard iO: Turing Machine Obfuscation and More*, ePrint 2026/1636.

title: Equivocal LWE from ordinary LWE
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Reduce Equivocal LWE to ordinary LWE, or find an attack separating the two assumptions.
status: Equivocal LWE was introduced as an additional assumption in the 2025 lattice-obfuscation construction.
why: This isolates a concrete dependency on one route toward plain-LWE iO.
key_works: Cini–Lai–Woo (2025), *Lattice-based Obfuscation from NTRU and Equivocal LWE*, ePrint 2025/1129.

title: Circular security with random opening from weaker assumptions
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Derive the circular-security-with-random-opening property used in lattice obfuscation from a more conventional circular-security assumption, with an explicit reduction.
status: The 2025 construction introduces a specialized property; ordinary circular encryption security is not an interchangeable assumption.
why: It would clarify whether a proposed simplification of iO assumptions is substantive.
key_works: Hsieh–Jain–Lin (2025), *Lattice-Based Post-Quantum iO from Circular Security with Random Opening Assumption*, ePrint 2025/390.

title: Non-lattice post-quantum iO
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Construct general iO from an independently studied post-quantum assumption family outside lattices, without importing an assumption already equivalent to obfuscation.
status: Existing well-founded constructions combine several ingredients; recent lattice candidates do not supply this assumption diversity.
why: It would reduce dependence on correlated failures within one mathematical platform.
key_works: Jain–Lin–Sahai (2021), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Well-Founded Assumptions*, DOI: 10.1145/3406325.3451093.

title: A defensible taxonomy of evasive-LWE assumptions
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Classify sampler access, public versus private coins, auxiliary information, and leakage conditions into regimes with valid reductions, explicit attacks, or genuinely unresolved status.
status: The 2025–2026 attacks invalidate several private-coin formulations; nearby definitions cannot safely inherit one another’s security.
why: It would prevent broken assumptions from reappearing under slightly changed notation.
key_works: Hsieh–Jain–Lin (2025), ePrint 2025/390; Huang–Hung–Yamada (2025/2026), *A Note on Obfuscation-Based Attacks on Private-Coin Evasive LWE*, ePrint 2025/421.

title: Cryptanalysis of all-product LWE
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Establish concrete security estimates or attacks for the all-product LWE assumption used in path-factorized functional encryption.
status: Diamond iO introduces this assumption; a construction paper is not independent cryptanalytic validation.
why: This assumption is a concentrated point of failure in an efficiency-oriented obfuscation proposal.
key_works: Suegami–Bottazzi–Park (2025, revised 2026), *Diamond iO: Indistinguishability Obfuscation at Near Functional-Encryption Cost via Matrix Products*, ePrint 2025/236.

title: Instantiating the pseudorandom-oracle step in efficient iO
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Replace the oracle-model component of an efficiency-oriented iO construction with an explicit standard-model primitive while preserving its security and asymptotic advantage.
status: Diamond iO’s transformation uses pseudorandom-oracle-model machinery; oracle replacement remains a separate obligation.
why: An efficient transformation in an idealized model is not yet a deployable obfuscator.
key_works: Suegami–Bottazzi–Park (2025/2026), *Diamond iO*, ePrint 2025/236.

title: Independently reproduced end-to-end general iO
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: **Proposed target:** implement an unrestricted iO candidate at explicit parameters, measuring generation, evaluation, peak memory, output size, and the cost of every assumed component.
status: Near-FE transformation cost does not establish practical end-to-end cost or an independently validated security margin.
why: It would reveal whether current candidates are limited by one component or by the entire construction.
key_works: Suegami–Bottazzi–Park (2025/2026), *Diamond iO*, ePrint 2025/236.

title: xiO from one-way functions
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Construct exponentially efficient iO from OWFs, achieving output size \(2^{(1-\varepsilon)n}\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,|C|)\) for a constant \(\varepsilon>0\).
status: The 2016 xiO framework isolates nontrivial compression, but an OWF-only construction remains unresolved.
why: Even partial truth-table compression could become a powerful intermediate cryptographic primitive.
key_works: Lin–Pass–Seth–Telang (2016), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation with Non-trivial Efficiency*, ePrint 2016/006.

title: xiO from plain LWE
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Obtain nontrivially compressing xiO from ordinary LWE without equivocal, evasive, or specialized circular assumptions.
status: New lattice obfuscation routes do not remove all additional assumptions, even when compression is used as an intermediate goal.
why: This is a potentially more accessible milestone than directly constructing polynomial-time iO.
key_works: Lin et al. (2016), ePrint 2016/006; Cini–Lai–Woo (2025), ePrint 2025/1129.

title: Polynomial-security xiO-to-iO lifting
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Upgrade polynomially secure xiO to polynomial-time iO without assuming subexponential security for xiO or its auxiliary primitives.
status: The foundational lifting theorem uses subexponential hardness.
why: It would make weak obfuscation constructions much more consequential.
key_works: Lin–Pass–Seth–Telang (2016), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation with Non-trivial Efficiency*, DOI: 10.1007/978-3-662-49387-8_17.

title: The computational compression frontier
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Determine tight tradeoffs among obfuscation time, output length, input length, and assumption strength for computationally secure compressing obfuscation.
status: Complexity classifications and statistical-security barriers leave multiple computational regimes unmatched.
why: It would identify which weak obfuscation goals are genuinely easier than full iO.
key_works: Asharov–Ephraim–Komargodski–Pass (2018/2022), *On the Complexity of Compressing Obfuscation*, ePrint 2018/552.

title: A semantic characterization of decomposable obfuscation
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Characterize decomposability through semantic properties of an obfuscator, rather than only through the syntax of particular constructions.
status: The decomposable-obfuscation framework supports important applications, but does not supply a complete classification of eligible obfuscators.
why: It would make application proofs less dependent on bespoke construction details.
key_works: Liu–Zhandry (2017/2021), *Decomposable Obfuscation: A Framework for Building Applications of Obfuscation from Polynomial Hardness*, DOI: 10.1007/s00145-021-09400-4.

title: Decomposable obfuscation directly from plain LWE
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Construct general-purpose decomposable obfuscation directly from ordinary LWE with polynomial security loss.
status: A framework showing what decomposability enables does not itself establish this assumption-specific construction.
why: It could enable useful obfuscation applications before the full plain-LWE iO problem is resolved.
key_works: Liu–Zhandry (2017/2021), *Decomposable Obfuscation*, DOI: 10.1007/s00145-021-09400-4.

title: Incrementally updatable obfuscation
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: **Proposed target:** update an obfuscated program after a small patch using work proportional to the changed region, while hiding unchanged secrets and patch history beyond declared leakage.
status: Decomposability alone is not an incremental-update security theorem.
why: It would permit maintained obfuscated software rather than immutable releases.
key_works: Liu–Zhandry (2017/2021), *Decomposable Obfuscation*, DOI: 10.1007/s00145-021-09400-4.

title: Fully succinct unrestricted obfuscation without additional helpers
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Obtain fully input-succinct unrestricted obfuscation from polynomially hard circuit iO without separately assuming succinct WE or suitable unique-proof succinct arguments.
status: Recent proof-restricted constructions identify additional ingredients for stronger succinctness.
why: Secret-program size could become largely independent of the eventual input-size bound.
key_works: Jain–Jin–Mathialagan–Paneth (2025/2026), *On Succinct Obfuscation via Propositional Proofs*, ePrint 2026/2009.

title: Proof-system dependence of obfuscation
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Determine whether moving from PV-provable equivalence to stronger proof systems changes the attainable power of obfuscation or only proof length and efficiency.
status: Modern proof-restricted constructions explicitly depend on the selected equivalence-proof system.
why: It would distinguish a technical limitation from a genuine hierarchy of cryptographic primitives.
key_works: Jain et al. (2025/2026), ePrint 2026/2009; Dujmovic et al. (2026), ePrint 2026/1636.

title: Practical equivalence certificates for proof-restricted obfuscation
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: **Proposed target:** automatically generate succinct, checkable equivalence proofs for realistic compiler transformations, with proof-generation cost comparable to compilation.
status: Polynomial-hardness PViO advances establish cryptographic possibilities, not a production compiler supplying the necessary certificates.
why: It would connect proof-restricted obfuscation to real software development.
key_works: Dujmovic–Hsieh–Jain–Quach (2026), *How to use Polynomially-Hard iO*, ePrint 2026/1636.

title: Public-coin diO without knowledge assumptions
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Construct public-coin differing-inputs obfuscation from iO and conventional assumptions without KOALA or another knowledge-style assumption.
status: An October 2026 preprint obtains public-coin diO from KOALA and iO.
why: It would strengthen obfuscation while avoiding assumptions about what an adversary “knows.”
key_works: Chen–Vaikuntanathan (2026), *Public-coin Differing-input Obfuscation from KOALA and iO*, ePrint 2026/2346.

title: The attainable auxiliary-input frontier for diO
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Characterize auxiliary-input generators for which differing-inputs obfuscation is attainable, with matching constructions and barriers for stronger generators.
status: Broad auxiliary-input formulations encounter implausibility results; restricting the sampler can materially change the question.
why: It would replace ambiguous “auxiliary-input security” claims with a usable classification.
key_works: Garg–Gentry–Halevi–Wichs (2014), *On the Implausibility of Differing-Inputs Obfuscation and Extractable Witness Encryption with Auxiliary Input*, ePrint 2013/860.

title: Structural classification of VBB-obfuscatable families
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Give necessary and sufficient conditions for broad natural function families to admit virtual-black-box obfuscation.
status: Universal VBB obfuscation is impossible; the unresolved task is classification between positive families and unobfuscatable examples.
why: It would identify where the strongest intuitive form of software secrecy is achievable.
key_works: Barak et al. (2001/2012), *On the (Im)possibility of Obfuscating Programs*, DOI: 10.1145/2160158.2160159.

title: Obfuscation for approximately equivalent randomized programs
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: **Proposed target:** protect randomized programs whose output distributions are close rather than identical, with explicit dependence on approximation error and repeated use.
status: Exact-equivalence iO does not automatically supply this guarantee; unrestricted VBB impossibility must still be respected.
why: Practical probabilistic and numerical software often lacks exact equivalence.
key_works: Barak et al. (2001/2012), *On the (Im)possibility of Obfuscating Programs*; Jain et al. (2025/2026), ePrint 2026/2009.

title: Stateful obfuscation with an explicit leakage boundary
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: **Proposed target:** characterize natural stateful program families that can hide internal state across adaptive interactions, resets, and forks, under a declared leakage model.
status: A stateless circuit-obfuscation theorem does not resolve state cloning, reset behavior, or persistent-history leakage.
why: Most useful services are interactive and stateful.
key_works: Barak et al. (2001/2012), *On the (Im)possibility of Obfuscating Programs*, DOI: 10.1145/2160158.2160159.

title: Sharp entropy thresholds for conjunction obfuscation
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Determine the minimum entropy conditions under which conjunction-obfuscation candidates remain secure, with matching attacks below the threshold.
status: Implementations under entropic Ring-LWE assumptions exist; security for arbitrary low-entropy conjunction distributions does not follow.
why: Real policies are frequently highly structured and nonuniform.
key_works: Cousins et al. (2017/2018), *Implementing Conjunction Obfuscation under Entropic Ring LWE*, ePrint 2017/844.

title: Conjunction obfuscation from ordinary Ring-LWE
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Remove the extra entropic assumption from a useful conjunction-obfuscation construction, or precisely delimit the distributions where ordinary Ring-LWE suffices.
status: The implemented entropic-Ring-LWE route leaves this assumption-reduction question separate.
why: It would strengthen one of the more concrete restricted-obfuscation approaches.
key_works: Cousins et al. (2017/2018), *Implementing Conjunction Obfuscation under Entropic Ring LWE*, DOI: 10.1109/SP.2018.00007.

title: Standard-model extractable WE for restricted samplers
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Construct extractable witness encryption for precisely specified public-coin or bounded-auxiliary-input samplers under conventional standard-model assumptions.
status: Generic-group extraction and knowledge-assumption constructions do not resolve this cleaner target.
why: Some applications need decryption capability to imply possession of an actual witness.
key_works: Campanelli (2026), *A Note on Extractable Witness Encryption in Generic Groups*, ePrint 2026/2399; Garg et al. (2014), ePrint 2013/860.

title: Collision resistance from iO and ordinary OWFs
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Construct collision-resistant hashing from iO and arbitrary OWFs without requiring rerandomizable OWFs or another extra primitive.
status: The 2026 rerandomization result obtains collision resistance under a stronger OWF condition.
why: It probes a major unresolved boundary of what iO implies.
key_works: Nassar (2026), *The Power of Rerandomization in Obfustopia*, ePrint 2026/1785; Asharov–Segev (2015), ePrint 2015/341.

title: Leakage-resilient obfuscator generation and execution
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: **Proposed target:** preserve security under quantified leakage from generation randomness, intermediate encodings, execution traces, and repeated physical observations.
status: Mathematical obfuscation definitions do not automatically cover these implementation interfaces.
why: A secure final artifact can still be compromised while being generated or executed.
key_works: Cousins et al. (2017/2018), *Implementing Conjunction Obfuscation under Entropic Ring LWE*, ePrint 2017/844.

title: Standard-model obfuscation of arbitrary quantum channels
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: Obfuscate arbitrary efficient quantum channels, including nonunitary operations, without an ideal classical oracle or pseudorandom-oracle idealization.
status: The 2026 arbitrary-channel construction is an oracle-model result.
why: It would extend general program secrecy to the full quantum-computation model.
key_works: Huang–Tang (2026), *Obfuscation of Arbitrary Quantum Circuits*, arXiv:2601.08969.

title: Classical descriptions of quantum obfuscations without oracle idealization
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: Obtain standard-model classical descriptions of obfuscated pseudodeterministic quantum circuits under explicit assumptions, without heuristic oracle replacement.
status: Publicly verifiable QFHE supplies an important oracle-model construction; it does not settle this instantiation problem.
why: Classical distribution would greatly simplify quantum-software deployment.
key_works: Bartusek–Gupte–Mutreja–Shmueli (2025/2026), *Classical Obfuscation of Quantum Circuits via Publicly-Verifiable QFHE*, arXiv:2510.08400.

title: Quantum iO from plain LWE beyond existing barriers
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: Construct a meaningful general quantum-iO variant from plain LWE using techniques outside the reduction classes excluded by recent barriers.
status: The 2026 falsifiable-assumption separation has specific interface and reduction restrictions.
why: It would connect quantum program secrecy to a conventional post-quantum assumption.
key_works: Barhoush–Morimae–Movassagh (2026), *Separating Quantum Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Falsifiable Assumptions*, arXiv:2608.25195.

title: Quantum-iO barriers against coherent reductions
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: Extend or evade the recent separation when a reduction makes coherent quantum queries rather than the restricted classical-query interface.
status: The query interface is a substantive qualification of the existing barrier.
why: It tests whether a remaining construction route is genuinely excluded.
key_works: Barhoush–Morimae–Movassagh (2026), *Separating Quantum Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Falsifiable Assumptions*, ePrint 2026/1800.

title: Quantum-state ciphertexts and quantum-iO barriers
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: Establish constructions or comparable impossibility results when the obfuscation or related witness-encryption ciphertext is a quantum state.
status: Classical-ciphertext restrictions leave a distinct resource regime outside the stated separation.
why: Quantum information may change the construction landscape, not merely the adversary.
key_works: Barhoush–Morimae–Movassagh (2026), arXiv:2608.25195.

title: Classical one-wayness from quantum iO
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: Identify which quantum-iO variants imply classical OWFs under weak worst-case assumptions, rather than only quantum-state cryptographic primitives.
status: The 2025 classification proves several quantum consequences; classical consequences depend on the variant.
why: It would clarify whether quantum obfuscation necessarily entails classical cryptographic hardness.
key_works: Morimae–Shirakawa–Yamakawa (2025/2026), *From Worst-Case Hardness of NP to Quantum Cryptography via Quantum Indistinguishability Obfuscation*, arXiv:2506.19542.

title: Single-copy versus multi-copy quantum-iO security
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: Prove implications or separations between one obfuscation state, polynomially many copies, and coherent evaluator access.
status: These interfaces supply different resources and cannot be identified by classical iO intuition alone.
why: Security should not silently change when protected programs are redistributed.
key_works: Morimae–Shirakawa–Yamakawa (2025/2026), arXiv:2506.19542.

title: Robust quantum obfuscation under implementation error
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: **Proposed target:** obtain guarantees stable under small diamond-norm implementation error, including entangled auxiliary inputs and repeated composition.
status: Exact channel functionality does not establish this fault-tolerant robustness statement.
why: Physical quantum gates never implement ideal channels exactly.
key_works: Huang–Tang (2026), *Obfuscation of Arbitrary Quantum Circuits*, arXiv:2601.08969.

title: Complete fault-tolerant resource estimates for quantum iO
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: **Proposed target:** derive logical-qubit counts, non-Clifford costs, memory lifetimes, and error budgets for an explicit quantum-obfuscation candidate.
status: Oracle-model constructions do not provide a complete physical implementation record.
why: It would reveal whether computation, storage, or error correction is the dominant obstacle.
key_works: Bartusek et al. (2025/2026), *Classical Obfuscation of Quantum Circuits via Publicly-Verifiable QFHE*, arXiv:2510.08400.

title: QMA witness encryption under conventional assumptions
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: Encrypt relative to QMA instances so that an appropriate quantum witness enables decryption, with an explicit consumable-witness or reusable-witness functionality.
status: Recent barriers distinguish ciphertext and reduction models; they do not settle every quantum-state construction.
why: Possession of quantum evidence could become a cryptographic access condition.
key_works: Barhoush–Morimae–Movassagh (2026), ePrint 2026/1800.

title: Unbounded-collusion public-key FE from plain LWE
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Construct public-key FE for all polynomial-size circuits with arbitrarily many polynomially bounded functional-key queries from ordinary LWE.
status: General FE and bounded-collusion FE exist; the clean-assumption, unrestricted-collusion combination remains unresolved.
why: It would enable expressive encrypted computation without general obfuscation assumptions.
key_works: Boneh–Sahai–Waters (2011), *Functional Encryption: Definitions and Challenges*, ePrint 2010/543.

title: Unbounded-collusion secret-key FE from OWFs
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Construct secret-key FE for general circuits from OWFs without fixing the number of issued functional keys at setup.
status: Minimal-assumption bounded-collusion results do not resolve the unbounded regime.
why: It would move a powerful class of selective-decryption capabilities toward minimal assumptions.
key_works: Boneh–Sahai–Waters (2011), *Functional Encryption: Definitions and Challenges*, DOI: 10.1007/978-3-642-19571-6_16.

title: General public-key FE from arbitrary PKE
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Derive unbounded-collusion general FE from ordinary public-key encryption, allowing non-black-box techniques.
status: Recent decentralized FE obtains bounded-collusion functionality from PKE but uses FE for the unbounded-collusion case.
why: It asks whether ordinary encryption already contains the power of arbitrary selective decryption.
key_works: Goyal–Yadugiri (2025/2026), *Decentralized Multi-Authority Functional Encryption with Malicious Authorities from Standard Assumptions*, ePrint 2025/412.

title: Succinct-encryption general FE from plain LWE
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Construct general FE whose encryption circuit and ciphertext size avoid dependence on a future maximum function size, under ordinary LWE.
status: Succinct encryption is a powerful strengthening: sufficiently secure FE with this property yields iO.
why: Data could be encrypted before the scale of future computations is known.
key_works: Bitansky–Vaikuntanathan (2015/2018), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Functional Encryption*, ePrint 2015/163; DOI: 10.1145/3234511.

title: Function-hiding general FE from lattices
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Hide both encrypted data and the functional key’s program, modulo unavoidable output leakage, for general circuits under plain lattice assumptions.
status: Restricted-family constructions and generic-group barriers do not settle general-circuit lattice function hiding.
why: It would protect proprietary models and queries as well as their input data.
key_works: Hajiabadi–Langrehr–Wang (2026), *Generic-Group Barriers for Function-Hiding and Multi-Input Functional Encryption*, ePrint 2026/1149.

title: The attainable simulation-security map for FE
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Characterize simulation-based FE security across adaptive keys, multiple messages, output leakage, and simulator resources, respecting known impossible regimes.
status: Indistinguishability security does not imply every simulation formulation; randomized-functionality work exposes important definitional gaps.
why: It would distinguish meaningful privacy promises from unattainable definitions.
key_works: Datta–Guan–Korb–Sahai (2025), *(Multi-Input) FE for Randomized Functionalities, Revisited*, ePrint 2025/330.

title: Strong randomized MIFE without subexponential iO
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Obtain adaptive randomized multi-input FE, secure against malicious encryptors and decryptors, without subexponential iO.
status: The 2025 construction supports unbounded messages per slot under subexponential iO; that functionality itself is no longer the open question.
why: Randomness should not become an unnoticed channel for exposing secrets.
key_works: Datta–Guan–Korb–Sahai (2025), *(Multi-Input) FE for Randomized Functionalities, Revisited*, ePrint 2025/330.

title: Compact FE with many corrupted authorities
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Achieve decentralized multi-authority FE with compact parameters and more than logarithmically many corrupted authorities without assuming general iO.
status: The 2026 revision identifies an iO implication for sufficiently compact high-corruption regimes; limited-corruption constructions do not settle them.
why: Decentralization should remain useful when many authorities are compromised.
key_works: Goyal–Yadugiri (2025/2026), ePrint 2025/412.

title: Dynamic decentralized FE with composable authority changes
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: **Proposed target:** support authority joins, departures, compromise, and recovery while preserving ciphertext validity and preventing cross-epoch key substitution.
status: Static authority guarantees do not by themselves establish this lifecycle functionality.
why: Real access-control systems change membership over years.
key_works: Goyal–Yadugiri (2025/2026), *Decentralized Multi-Authority Functional Encryption with Malicious Authorities*, ePrint 2025/412.

title: Large-domain MCFE from minimal assumptions
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Extend minimal-assumption small-domain multi-client FE to exponentially large domains without an exponential encoding expansion.
status: The 2025–2026 small-domain result has domain, arity, and query-bound qualifications.
why: Long records, identifiers, and numerical encodings naturally require large domains.
key_works: Biswas–Vaid–Yerukhimovich (2025/2026), *Multi-Client Functional Encryption for Small Domains*, ePrint 2025/2210.

title: Tensor-preimage-hint security from ordinary LWE
subfield: Restricted FE, attribute-based encryption, and registration
open: Reduce the higher-degree tensor-preimage-hint assumption used in polynomial FE to ordinary LWE, or give a separating attack.
status: The 2026 construction reduces degree one to LWE; higher degrees require a new assumption.
why: It would establish a standard-assumption foundation for useful low-degree FE.
key_works: Cini–Lai–Ünal–Woo (2026), *Lattice-based Secret-Key Functional Encryption for Constant-Degree Polynomials*, ePrint 2026/1977.

title: Public-key quadratic FE from plain LWE
subfield: Restricted FE, attribute-based encryption, and registration
open: Construct unbounded-collusion public-key FE for general quadratic functions from ordinary LWE with polynomial-size parameters.
status: Secret-key low-degree lattice candidates do not establish this public-key, plain-LWE target.
why: Quadratic functions already support covariance, similarity, and many statistical computations.
key_works: Cini–Lai–Ünal–Woo (2026), *Lattice-based Secret-Key Functional Encryption for Constant-Degree Polynomials*, ePrint 2026/1977.

title: Adaptive constant-degree lattice FE
subfield: Restricted FE, attribute-based encryption, and registration
open: Upgrade the selective-security constant-degree lattice FE candidate to adaptive security without prohibitive security loss or stronger assumptions.
status: The 2026 construction’s selective-security qualification remains substantive.
why: Users choose later computations after observing earlier outputs.
key_works: Cini–Lai–Ünal–Woo (2026), ePrint 2026/1977.

title: Compact post-quantum function-hiding quadratic FE
subfield: Restricted FE, attribute-based encryption, and registration
open: Obtain compact function-hiding quadratic FE under post-quantum assumptions without impractically expanding the problem into inner-product dimensions.
status: Function hiding, quadratic expressiveness, and compactness are separate requirements; generic-group barriers constrain simple extensions.
why: It would protect useful statistical models as well as their inputs.
key_works: Hajiabadi–Langrehr–Wang (2026), *Generic-Group Barriers for Function-Hiding and Multi-Input Functional Encryption*, ePrint 2026/1149.

title: Fully tight lattice inner-product FE
subfield: Restricted FE, attribute-based encryption, and registration
open: Remove remaining reduction losses in lattice IPFE while preserving compactness and the relevant adaptive security guarantees.

subfield: SNARG and SNARK foundations

subfield: SNARG and SNARK foundations

subfield: Coding theory and practical transparent post-quantum proofs

status: This is a distinct quantitative challenge from mutual correlated agreement.

key_works: Arnon–Boneh–Fenzi (2026), *Open Problems in List Decoding and Correlated Agreement*, ePrint 2026/680.

title: Bit-efficient Reed–Solomon decoding near capacity
subfield: Coding theory and practical transparent post-quantum proofs
open: Obtain the relevant near-capacity decoding guarantees with time polynomial in \(n\) and \(\log q\), rather than polynomial in the field size \(q\).
status: A September 2026 preprint reports fixed-slack prime-field decoding with \(q^{O_\gamma(1)}\) running time.

title: Shrinking-slack proximity-gap tradeoffs
subfield: Coding theory and practical transparent post-quantum proofs
open: Determine tight list-size and agreement bounds as the gap to capacity shrinks with block length, rather than remaining constant.
status: Fixed-slack positive results coexist with near-capacity counterexamples; the parameter regimes must not be conflated.

key_works: Jeronimo (2026), arXiv:2609.05870; Krachun–Kazanin–Haböck (2026), *Failure of Proximity Gaps Close to Capacity*, ePrint 2026/782.

title: Sound small-characteristic code regimes after counterexamples
subfield: Coding theory and practical transparent post-quantum proofs
open: Characterize small-characteristic extension-code families and parameter ranges that admit strong enough list-size and distance-preservation bounds for practical proofs.
status: Recent attacks show that optimistic blanket small-field assumptions are false.
why: Small fields are attractive for speed but can alter the soundness calculation.
key_works: Fenzi–Sanso (2025/2026), *Small-field Hash-based SNARGs Are Less Sound Than Conjectured*, ePrint 2025/2197.

title: Sharp concrete FRI soundness beyond classical thresholds
subfield: Coding theory and practical transparent post-quantum proofs
open: Derive independently checked finite-parameter soundness bounds with explicit constants, query counts, and composition losses in useful beyond-Johnson regimes.
status: A 2026 preprint proposes threshold-halving bounds; practical optimality and complete-stack calibration remain separate obligations.

key_works: Chai–Fan (2026), *FRI Soundness Above the Johnson Bound via Threshold Halving*, ePrint 2026/858.

title: Sub-10-kilobyte lattice polynomial commitments
subfield: Coding theory and practical transparent post-quantum proofs

why: It would narrow an important usability gap between lattice and pairing-based proof systems.
key_works: Dao et al. (2026), *Akita: A High-Performance Lattice-Based Polynomial Commitment Scheme*, ePrint 2026/1983.

title: Efficient polylogarithmic verification for lattice commitments
subfield: Coding theory and practical transparent post-quantum proofs
open: Obtain genuinely polylogarithmic verification with practical constants, near-linear proving, and compact lattice proofs.
status: Akita offers tunable \(N^{1/K}\)-type verification for fixed \(K\); this is not the same as a practical polylogarithmic bound.
why: Verifiers should remain inexpensive as committed computations grow.
key_works: Dao et al. (2026), *Akita*, ePrint 2026/1983.

title: Tiny fully post-quantum recursive proofs
subfield: Coding theory and practical transparent post-quantum proofs
open: **Proposed moonshot:** achieve recursively composable proofs below roughly one kilobyte with practical proving and verification, without a pairing-based final wrapper.
status: Post-quantum small-field folding exists; the complete tiny-proof target is stronger.
why: Long proof histories could become cheap to transmit and verify.
key_works: Nguyen–Setty (2026), *Neo and SuperNeo: Post-quantum Folding with Pay-per-bit Costs over Small Fields*, ePrint 2026/242.

title: Optimal streamed-prover time–space tradeoffs
subfield: Coding theory and practical transparent post-quantum proofs
open: Determine optimal prover time and memory for computations with low-space witness generation, counting stream generation, rereads, and commitment work.
status: Hobbit already achieves optimal prover time in its model; stronger memory bounds must not omit the cost of supplying the stream.
why: Large proofs should not require unaccounted execution-trace storage.
key_works: Pappas–Papadopoulos (2025), *Hobbit: Space-Efficient zkSNARK with Optimal Prover Time*, ePrint 2025/1214.

title: OWFs from \(P\neq NP\)
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions

why: It would connect basic cryptography to a central complexity conjecture.

title: Post-quantum OWFs from quantum worst-case hardness
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Derive classical functions hard to invert quantumly from a natural worst-case assumption such as appropriate NP hardness against quantum computation, without quantum iO.
status: Quantum-iO-based implications do not establish the bare worst-case implication.
why: It would give a foundational explanation for post-quantum cryptography.
key_works: Morimae–Shirakawa–Yamakawa (2025/2026), arXiv:2506.19542.

title: Collision-resistant hashing from arbitrary OWFs
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Construct collision-resistant hashing from arbitrary OWFs without stronger algebraic assumptions or an obfuscation helper.
status: Black-box barriers and conditional advances do not settle unrestricted constructions.
why: Collision resistance supports commitments, authentication, and succinct proofs.
key_works: Asharov–Segev (2015), *Limits on the Power of Indistinguishability Obfuscation and Functional Encryption*, ePrint 2015/341.

title: Classical key agreement from OWFs beyond black-box methods
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Construct classical key agreement from OWFs through non-black-box techniques, or establish a stronger barrier.
status: The foundational 1989 black-box separation remains compatible with unresolved non-black-box possibilities.

key_works: Impagliazzo–Rudich (1989), *Limits on the Provable Consequences of One-Way Permutations*, DOI: 10.1145/73007.73012; Barnum–Heath (2026), ePrint 2026/113.

title: Classical oblivious transfer from arbitrary PKE
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions

key_works: Gertner–Kannan–Malkin–Reingold–Viswanathan (2000), *The Relationship between Public Key Encryption and Oblivious Transfer*, DOI: 10.1109/SFCS.2000.892121.

title: Standard-model oblivious interactive hashing from OWFs
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Construct the oblivious interactive hash primitive from OWFs in the standard model.
status: The 2026 work constructs it from random oracles and from OT, and derives OT non-black-box from a standard-model instance; it does not construct OT from a random oracle.
why: It offers a sharply formulated intermediate target for crossing classical cryptographic boundaries.
key_works: Barnum–Heath (2026), *How to Steal Oblivious Transfer from Minicrypt*, ePrint 2026/113.

title: Distributional collision resistance from OWFs
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Construct distributional collision-resistant hashing from arbitrary OWFs, or strengthen the known separation evidence.
status: This weaker collision notion supports useful primitives not known from OWFs alone.
why: It could bridge part of the gap between inversion hardness and collision resistance.
key_works: Bitansky–Haitner–Komargodski–Yogev (2019), *Distributional Collision Resistance Beyond One-Way Functions*, DOI: 10.1007/978-3-030-17659-4_23.

title: Monotone distributional collision resistance from dCRH
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions

status: The 2026 result constructs monotone dCRH from CRH; weakening the assumption remains a distinct target.
why: It would clarify the minimum negation complexity required by cryptographic hardness.
key_works: Puniamurthy (2026), *A Note on the Existence of Monotone Distributional Collision Resistant Hash Functions*, IACR CiC 3(1), article 11.

title: Negation complexity of second-preimage resistance
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Determine tight negation requirements for second-preimage-resistant families and their relationship to monotone distributional collision resistance.
status: Existing monotonicity results distinguish OWFs, CRH, and dCRH rather than providing a complete classification.
why: It would expose structural differences between related hardness notions.
key_works: Puniamurthy (2026), *A Note on the Existence of Monotone Distributional Collision Resistant Hash Functions*.

title: Efficiently samplable pseudorandomness from worst-case meta-complexity
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions

status: The 2026 implications carefully distinguish conditional pseudorandomness from an ordinary efficiently usable PRG.
why: It would move worst-case hardness closer to deployable cryptography.
key_works: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2026), *Cryptographic Implications of Worst-Case Hardness of Time-Bounded Kolmogorov Complexity*, ePrint 2026/668.

title: Stronger zero knowledge from worst-case meta-complexity

status: The 2026 results establish qualified forms, not every conventional efficient zero-knowledge guarantee.
why: It would strengthen the bridge from worst-case complexity to cryptographic protocols.
key_works: Liu–Mazor–Pass (2026), *Cryptographic Implications of Worst-Case Hardness of Time-Bounded Kolmogorov Complexity*, ePrint 2026/668.

title: A natural concrete instance of genuine Microcrypt
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Find a natural quantum cryptographic assumption plausibly weaker than classical OWFs, with evidence that it does not secretly imply them.

why: It would demonstrate a genuinely weaker quantum foundation rather than disguised classical hardness.
key_works: Carrasco et al. (2026), *Instantiating Microcrypt: Obstacles and Opportunities via Tailored State Certification*, arXiv:2609.15842.

title: Multi-copy pseudorandom states from general quantum one-wayness
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Derive reusable multi-copy pseudorandom states from general efficiently verifiable quantum one-wayness, allowing non-black-box techniques.
status: Quantum one-wayness lacks the complete OWF-to-PRG equivalence available classically.
why: It would identify a minimal foundation for quantum pseudorandomness.
key_works: Cavalar–Goldin–Gray–Hall–Liu–Pelecanos (2025), *On the Computational Hardness of Quantum One-Wayness*, DOI: 10.22331/q-2025-03-27-1679.

title: The copy threshold for unconditional quantum one-wayness
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Sharpen the transition between copy-bounded information-theoretic one-wayness and regimes requiring computational hardness.
status: Known unconditional and computational regimes leave a quantitative threshold question rather than a simple yes/no equivalence.
why: It would identify precisely when quantum cryptography begins to require computational assumptions.
key_works: Cavalar et al. (2025), *On the Computational Hardness of Quantum One-Wayness*, DOI: 10.22331/q-2025-03-27-1679.

title: Many-time QCCC signatures from minimal puzzles
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Identify the weakest puzzle assumption sufficient for many-time signatures with quantum computation and classical communication.
status: Recent one-time equivalences and oracle separations do not establish the same many-time hierarchy.
why: Reusable authentication is essential for meaningful cryptographic systems.
key_works: Chen–Wang–Xie (2026), *The Breakdown of Classical Minicrypt Equivalences in the Quantum-Computation Classical-Communication Model*, arXiv:2609.33098.

title: QCCC commitments from general efficiently verifiable puzzles
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Remove additional distributional restrictions from puzzle-based QCCC commitment constructions, or prove the restrictions necessary.

why: Commitments are a gateway to richer quantum-classical protocols.
key_works: Chen–Wang–Xie (2026), arXiv:2609.33098.

key_works: Boneh–Zhandry (2014/2017), *Multiparty Key Exchange, Efficient Traitor Tracing, and More from Indistinguishability Obfuscation*, ePrint 2013/642.
